references.text: The Levites were to eat their portion of the offerings in any clean place, illustrating the principle that servants of the sanctuary could enjoy their share anywhere.
The Levites were to eat their portion of the tithe together with their households, confirming that their families were also included in this blessing.
The Levites had no inheritance in the land, but the Lord himself was their inheritance, and they received their wages through service at the sanctuary.
The tithe was given to the Levites as payment for their service in the Tent of Meeting, and this is the broader context for the verse.
Paul refers to the principle that those who serve at the altar should live from the altar, just as the Levites received their wages for their service.
Jesus teaches that the worker is worthy of his food, a principle that reflects the Levites' right to receive payment for their service.
Paul quotes the principle that the worker deserves his wages, which has its root in God's arrangement for the support of the Levites.
The priests were to eat from the sin offering in a holy place, but the tithe could be eaten anywhere, showing the difference between various types of offerings.
